transcript.text: Bosch integrated dishwasher showing E:15 and the pump keeps running. Model SMV4HTX31E. I've turned it off and on, still there

E:15 with the drain pump running continuously means the Bosch anti-flood protection has operated. The pump itself is usually not the fault: it is being held on because water has reached the base tray. Switching it off and on will not clear it while the float still detects water. Most likely causes are a leak or excessive foam; less commonly, the base float is stuck. Do not keep trying to run programmes, as any continuing leak can refill the base. 1. Turn it off at the mains, unplug or isolate it, and close the water tap.
2. Check around the door seal and lower door edge for dirt, damage or anything trapped in it. Also check that the lower spray arm is not split and can turn without hitting dishes.
3. Under the sink, check the inlet-hose and drain-hose connections for drips, loose fittings or splits. Look for excess foam as well—washing-up liquid or the wrong detergent can create enough foam to trigger this fault. If those areas are dry and sound, the water is likely from an internal leak, such as a pump/sump seal or internal hose. An engineer will need to trace that safely; simply drying the base may make it run briefly, but does not cure the leak. The flood switch should only be suspected if the base is proven dry.

Door seal looks okay, and I only use tablets so there's no foam. No water on the kitchen floor either. I can't pull the unit out because it's fully integrated under the worktop, so I can't check the hose connections behind it. The socket is in the cupboard next to it, so I can unplug it from there. I haven't checked the spray arm.

No water on the kitchen floor does not rule this out: E:15 commonly occurs when a small internal leak is caught safely in the base tray, which is why the drain pump keeps running. With no foam and the door seal appearing sound, an internal sump/pump seal or hose leak is now the leading possibility. Before arranging an engineer, check the lower spray arm, as a split arm can throw water sideways and trigger the same protection. 1. Unplug the dishwasher from the adjacent cupboard socket.
2. Pull out the lower rack and turn the lower spray arm by hand. Make sure no dish or rack item could have been catching it.
3. Inspect the arm, especially its underside and seam, for a fine split, crack, loose section or blocked jets. If it is cracked or split, that is a likely source and should be dealt with before using the dishwasher again. If it is intact and turns freely, the remaining likely cause is an internal leak rather than the drain pump or flood switch. Because the machine is integrated and accessing the base requires removal/dismantling, an appliance engineer is the sensible next step; ask them to trace the source of the E:15 base-tray leak rather than simply reset or dry the tray.
[Helpful to see: image "Check and rinse the spray arm" — The spray arm spins to fire water through small jet holes. Check it spins freely and rinse the jets clear of food/grit. It usually unclips at the centre. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
I'm not sure how to tell if the spray arm is split, I can't see anything obvious on it. Is an engineer the next step then?

Yes — an engineer is the sensible next step. E:15 and a continuously running drain pump indicate the base-water protection has operated. As there is no obvious foam, door-seal issue or visible spray-arm damage, the most likely cause is a small internal leak, commonly from a sump/pump seal or an internal hose/joint. A split spray arm is usually visible as a crack, opening along its seam, or a loose section; not seeing anything obvious makes that less likely, though it cannot be ruled out completely. Keep the dishwasher unplugged and the water tap closed, and do not keep restarting programmes. Ask the engineer to remove the integrated machine, inspect the base tray for water, and trace the source of the E:15 leak — rather than only drying/resetting the base tray. Drying it may clear the fault briefly, but will not cure an underlying leak.

candidates: Water in the base tray has activated the anti-flood system, usually due to a leak or excess foam (high)
Flood float/switch stuck despite a dry base (low)
